summary: The candidate removes the unsynchronized global prefix reload by deriving each expert offset from token counts already in registers. The recorded base fails the structural/IR regression; the exact candidate passes its regression and independent guarded randomized GPU references. No code-level counterexample was found under the kernel's padded-segment contract.

tests.what_was_measured: Failing-before: 5/5 failures identified the source reload and compiled TTIR load marker; numerical references happened to pass on gfx950.
Base output/prefix/sentinel comparison and compiler IR. No runtime corruption appeared on gfx950, while TTIR retained the unsafe reload.
Candidate regression: 5/5 AST, GPU numerical reference, boundary, and compiled-TTIR cases passed.
120 independent randomized guarded GPU launches across 2-129 experts and block sizes 16-128; exact prefix/index references, both output guards, and absence of the TTIR reload.

gpu_execution.evidence: One AMD Instinct MI355X, gfx950:sramecc+:xnack-, ran all numerical and guarded probes; raw logs and emitted gfx950 ISA are retained.

remaining_limitations: The supplied GPU was AMD gfx950, not the report's NVIDIA H20, so NVIDIA PTX scheduling and the exact CUDA illegal-memory-access symptom were not reproduced.
No full model weights or multi-node DeepEP deployment were available, so the downstream CPU recv timeout chain was not exercised.

The base race did not manifest as numerical corruption in 1000 guarded gfx950 launches; failing-before proof is the source/compiled-IR hazard plus the deterministic regression, not a fabricated runtime crash.
No native rebuild was applicable because the candidate changes only Triton Python and tests.
